title: Algebraic Proportions
objectives: Set up and solve percent equations with unknowns
Apply proportional reasoning to real-world problems

introduction.context: If a recipe for 4 people calls for 2 cups of flour, how much flour do you need for 6 people? This scaling problem uses algebraic proportions!
introduction.connection: Proportions with variables help us solve problems involving scaling recipes, calculating discounts, determining medication dosages, and converting between units.

concepts.title: Algebraic Proportions
concepts.content: An equation stating that two ratios are equal, where at least one ratio contains a variable. Like arithmetic proportions, but now we solve for unknown values using algebra.

concepts.title: Cross-Multiplication
concepts.content: Multiplying diagonally across a proportion to create an equation to solve. If a/b = c/d, then ad = bc. This works even when variables are involved.

practice.explanation: Set up proportion: 5/25 = x/100. Cross-multiply: 500 = 25x, so x = 20%.
hints: Set up as a proportion with 100
5 out of 25 is what out of 100?
